controversies.category: PILOT Tax Abatements & School Funding Exclusion
controversies.title: PILOT Tax Breaks vs. School District Revenues in Montclair Township
controversies.entityInvolved: Township of Montclair (Municipal Government) vs. Montclair Public Schools
controversies.summary: Long-term tax exemptions granted to major developments along commercial corridors bypass the school district (which normal takes 57.2% of property taxes), forcing existing homeowners to absorb student enrollment costs.
controversies.investigationDetails: Under New Jersey's Long Term Tax Exemption Law (N.J.S.A. 40A:20), municipalities can grant 30-year PILOTs where the developer pays an Annual Service Charge directly to Town Hall (95%) and the County (5%), while the public school district receives $0 statutory share. In Montclair Township, where schools consume 57.2% of standard taxes, each new luxury residential unit adds student load without contributing ad valorem school tax support.
controversies.taxpayerImpact: Millions in abated school taxes shifted directly onto single-family homeowners across Montclair Township.
controversies.status: Active community oversight and school board revenue-sharing debate.

controversies.title: School District Deficit Crisis, Infrastructure Bonds & Lackawanna PILOT Protests
controversies.summary: Recurring multi-million dollar public school structural budget deficits, an $188M school bond referendum, and fierce community opposition over 30-year PILOT tax breaks at Lackawanna Plaza and Seymour Street.
controversies.investigationDetails: With inflation pushing employee healthcare past $64.2M and commercial ratables under pressure (16.8% of the tax base), Montclair Township has had to manage tax levy growth against the 2% statutory cap, leading to school and municipal fiscal tension.
controversies.taxpayerImpact: Homeowners fund 83.2% of the property tax check, heightening public scrutiny on every budget line item.
controversies.status: Ongoing legislative and budget audit monitoring.
